qs.q:
Personal Computers — Which person…

A=Vanessa (runs firm from home, emails clients, internet banking, internet calls to America)
B=Alex (teacher, uses PC increasingly in classroom, lesson preparation, teaching forums)
C=Pete (leisure use, reads news sites, no credit card, partner criticises time online)
D=Sue (laptop, commutes with it, family rule: no PC at home in flat)

F=Mohammed (writing thesis, back-up copies, emails tutor, doesn't know world news)

0. says they can carry their PC very easily? [D=Sue: 'it's so light I can use it while commuting']
1. gets advice from the internet?
2. doesn't use their PC at home?
3. tries to control how much time they spend on their PC?
4. says they don't need so many meetings now?
5. uses their PC instead of the telephone?
6. uses their PC to find out what's happening in the world?
7. uses their PC when travelling?
8. makes and receives payments on their PC?
9. uses their PC in the workplace more than they used to?
10. says their PC saves them space?
11. says someone criticises how long they spend on their PC?
12. doesn't give information about themselves over the internet?
items: 2 — doesn't use their PC at home?
3 — tries to control how much time they spend on their PC?
4 — says they don't need so many meetings now?
5 — uses their PC instead of the telephone?
6 — uses their PC to find out what's happening in the world?
8 — makes and receives payments on their PC?
9 — uses their PC in the workplace more than they used to?
10 — says their PC saves them space?
11 — says someone criticises how long they spend on their PC?
12 — doesn't give information about themselves over the internet?

qs.q:
Is Competitive Sport a Good Thing?

"What initially came to mind was that maybe it occupies too many hours of the school timetable. I know that some parents complain that it distracts children from their studies."

At first, the writer thought that some schools had banned competitive sport because…
A it has a negative psychological impact.
B there are a lot of injuries.
C pupils already do enough exercise.
D it takes up too much time.
opts: it has a negative psychological impact.
there are a lot of injuries.
it takes up too much time.

qs.q:
Is Competitive Sport a Good Thing?

"I recall that we came last but one out of twelve teams in our league."

In which position did the writer's football team finish in their league?
A First.
B Second.
C Eleventh.
D Last.

Is Competitive Sport a Good Thing?

"Did the experience damage us mentally? I'm still in contact with quite a few of the people who I played with and they appear to have grown up without any lasting effects."

The example of the writer's football team is used to show how…
A pointless certain organised sports can be.
B team sports can help keep young people fit.
C losing doesn't necessarily matter to children.
D team sports can help bring people together.
opts: pointless certain organised sports can be.
team sports can help keep young people fit.
losing doesn't necessarily matter to children.
team sports can help bring people together.

qs.q:
Is Competitive Sport a Good Thing?

"Competition is part of life, so surely it's better to prepare pupils for this rather than protect them from such realities. Learning how to manage both success and failure is a vital lesson."

According to paragraph three, competitive sport can help pupils…
A work successfully in teams.
B cope with life's disappointments.
C perform better at school.
D get a good job after their education.
opts: get a good job after their education.

qs.q:
Is Competitive Sport a Good Thing?

"The result was much better than either I or my trainer had ever expected and was one that was never to be repeated. In fact, it's a result that I still look back on with a certain amount of pride."

The main point in paragraph four is that…
A bad results can help motivate people.
B losing is not necessarily the same as failure.
C sport is a source of pride for people.
D many people no longer play sport as adults.
opts: bad results can help motivate people.
losing is not necessarily the same as failure.
sport is a source of pride for people.
many people no longer play sport as adults.

qs.q:
Is Competitive Sport a Good Thing?

"That's not to say that activities like aerobics or Pilates are bad. On the contrary, any kind of exercise is a good thing in the modern world that we live in."

The writer says that non-competitive physical activities in school…
A can have some positive effects.
B are an up-to-date innovation.
C are disappointing in the short run.
D should not have prizes.
opts: are disappointing in the short run.

qs.q:
Dealing with homework

"First, make sure you understand the assignment. (19) ___. It's much easier to take a minute to ask the teacher than to struggle later that night!"

A Naturally, this can make them hate a class.
B Don't be afraid to clarify what's expected.
C Instead, ask an adult or older sibling for help.
D Therefore it's a good idea to come up with some kind of homework schedule.
E However, this might not get you the results you need.
F So it's best to use this mental power on the subjects that are most challenging.
G But what if you don't feel comfortable with your teacher?
H As a result, you will become less productive than if you stop every so often.
opts: A — Naturally, this can make them hate a class.
B — Don't be afraid to clarify what's expected.
C — Instead, ask an adult or older sibling for help.
D — Come up with some kind of homework schedule.
E — However, this might not get you the results you need.

G — But what if you don't feel comfortable with your teacher?
H — You will become less productive than if you stop every so often.
